description.value: The study investigated neural and emotional substrates of accepting anger-infused ultimatum offers during dynamic social interactions using a modified repeated Ultimatum Game during fMRI.

value: vmPFC activity will differentiate between individuals with high or low monetary gains accumulated throughout the game and reflect a divergence in the associated emotional experience.
We hypothesized that high-gainers would report less anger, and exhibit less sympathetic arousal compared to low-gainers.
We also hypothesized that increased activity in this region would relate both to high-gain and reduced anger.
Finally, since unfair offers induce more anger, we expected the behavioral and neural effects to be more accentuated during such offers compared to fair offers.

description.value: Prospective first-time-point study of healthy male civilians and soldiers using a repeated, dynamic Ultimatum Game during fMRI.

spans.text: ### Modified Ultimatum Game

description.value: Participants played repeated ultimatum-game rounds with verbal negotiations and fair or unfair offers from a putative proposer.
Fair ultimatum offers allocating 10:10, 11:9, or 12:8 ILS between proposer and responder; participants decided whether to accept or reject each offer.
Unfair ultimatum offers allocating 15:5, 16:4, 17:3, 18:2, or 19:1 ILS between proposer and responder; participants decided whether to accept or reject each offer.

spans.text: Participants played the responder and were led to believe that their decisions to accept or reject (via a button press) were made vis-à-vis offers by a proposer

instructions.value: Participants played the responder in a repeated ultimatum game, deciding by button press whether to accept or reject offers from a putative proposer. They were told that verbal negotiations could be used to bargain with the proposer and maximize monetary gain, and that the proposer supposedly split 20 ILS in real time.

stimuli.value: Photographs of the putative proposer and the participant's photograph as a negotiation cue, monetary ultimatum offers, outcome displays, and 30-second verbal negotiations with an obnoxious professional-actor confederate proposer.

caption.value: The four sequences of offers used in the modified UG.

footer.value: The four sequences of offers used in the modified UG included 10 offers each, allotted from a pot of 20 New Israeli Shekel (ILS). Sequences were counterbalanced between participants. In order to minimize artifacts of head-movement, the sequences were divided into two seamless functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging (fMRI) scans. The 1st and 2nd fMRI scans of the 1st sequence were switched in order in the 2nd sequence, while the 1st and 2nd fMRI scans of the 3rd sequence were switched in order in the 4th sequence.

caption.value: Reliability, gain-groups differences and correlations with vmPFC for trait questionnaires.

footer.value: As part of the prospective study we acquired various personality questionnaires of which we provide general details, including number of participants who completed the questionnaire (denoted by #), reliability, Student's t-test comparing between gain-groups, and correlation with vmPFC activity during the offer period. ^ denotes that one item was removed because it impacted reliability and * denotes significance at an uncorrected two-tailed p-value. In NEO-Agreeableness, low-gainers (LGs; 29.04 ± 3.87, mean ± SD) had a lower average score compared to high-gainers (HGs; 31.55 ± 4.89). The last measure refers to a post-scan self-report of participants' desire to gain money in the game. Numbered notes 3–10 are referenced below at the Supplementary References; p-values are two-tailed uncorrected.

caption.value: Statistical results for recruitment-group (civilians/soldiers), sequence of offers (1/2/3/4) and actors (1/2/3) factors.

footer.value: ANOVA results showing that the recruitment-group (civilians/soldiers), sequence of offers (1/2/3/4) and actors (1/2/3) did not have an influence on (A) acceptance rates, (B) reaction times, (C) emotional ratings — here we specifically tested whether these factors influenced the interaction found between potency (low/high) and valence (positive/negative); and (D–E) skin conductance response (SCR) measures. LGs = low-gainers, HGs = high-gainers; p-values are two-tailed uncorrected.
